## 5-Year Investment Growth Snapshot

A $12,000 lump sum grows differently depending on return and risk. With annual compounding and no extra contributions, the higher-return option also carries the most volatility.

## Estimated Ending Values by Investment Choice

| Option | Annual Return | Risk Level | Ending Value | Total Gain |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| High-yield savings account | 4.2% APY | Low | $14,676.36 | $2,676.36 |
| Bond fund | 5.1% avg. annually | Moderate | $15,358.47 | $3,358.47 |
| Broad stock index fund | 8.0% avg. annually | High | $17,626.10 | $5,626.10 |

### Risk Comparison
- **High-yield savings account:** Lowest risk; principal is typically stable, but returns are modest and may change with interest rates.
- **Bond fund:** Moderate risk; can fluctuate with interest rates and credit conditions, but usually less volatile than stocks.
- **Broad stock index fund:** Highest risk; values can swing significantly year to year, but it offers the best long-term growth potential of the three.
